newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Indian sub-continent demand seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Indian sub-continent demand seen mixed.

text.p: India's continuing political uncertainty is expected to keep gold prices firm in the current week while in neighbouring Pakistan a slump in demand may push them further down, dealers said on Monday.
A new prime minister assumed office at the head of a centre-left coalition government in India on Monday but dealers said it would take some time for things to get back to normal.
The new incumbent, Inder Kumar Gujral, who replaced Prime Minister Deve Gowda in the 13-party coalition government after its defeat last week, is seeking a confidence vote on Tuesday.
"The marriage season has a bigger impact on demand and supply of gold than the current political crisis," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani.
In the week to Monday standard gold rose 25 rupees to 4,830 on the Bombay bullion market.
Dealers said they expected supplies of imported gold to rise following the conclusion of the Moslem festival of Eid al-Adha in the Gulf where a large number of Indians are employed.
"Indian expatriates in the Gulf are bringing gold after a brief lull," said Damani. "I expect the improved supplies to be met with matching demand."
"Marriage season demand is good. I expect prices to be steady to firm in the near term," Damani said.
In Pakistan's chief commercial city of Karachi gold prices are likely to fall further this week due to low demand after Eid al-Adha, dealers said.
"Gold prices are likely to ease marginally this week as demand usually declines after festivals like Eid al-Adha," dealer Jan Mohammad said.
"Today there is little trading activity because people are still in a holiday mood," another dealer said. Pakistani markets re-opened on Monday after a four-day break for Eid al-Adha.

In Dubai, a gold re-export market, prices fell in line with sharply lower international bullion rates in the week to Sunday, but traders said political turmoil in India had helped keep prices in the emirate from slipping further.

"There is good moderate demand from India. Because of the political scene there the market is a bit better than it would have been. It would have been lower if there hadn't been the political upheaval in India," said one trader.
Dubai is the main feeder market for gold into the subcontinent. India is the world's single largest gold market.
Traders said even though some shipments to the subcontinent had been slowed down by the four-day Eid al-Adha Moslem holiday in Dubai, demand was still evident.
